TEXT
Globalisation has turned the world into a small village where goods, ideas and people move freely across borders. Thanks to it, we can buy products from all over the world, watch foreign films and communicate with people from different cultures. Globalisation has helped many developing countries grow by opening new markets and creating jobs. However, it also has a darker side. Small local businesses often cannot compete with huge international companies and are forced to close. Rich countries sometimes become richer while poor ones stay poor. Moreover, some people fear that globalisation is destroying local cultures and traditions, as everyone starts to eat the same food, wear the same clothes and speak the same language. The challenge is to enjoy the benefits of globalisation without losing our identity.

I. READING COMPREHENSION (8 marks)
1) How has globalisation turned the world into "a small village"?   (2 marks)
2) How has globalisation helped developing countries?   (2 marks)
3) Give two negative effects of globalisation mentioned in the text.   (2 marks)
4) What is "the challenge" mentioned at the end?   (2 marks)

II. LANGUAGE (6 marks)
1) Put into the present perfect: Globalisation (turn) ______ the world into a small village.   (1,5 marks)
2) Complete with a linker (however / because): Globalisation has benefits; ______, it also has a darker side.   (1,5 marks)
3) Give the comparative: Rich countries become ______ (rich) while poor ones stay poor.   (1,5 marks)
4) Give the opposite of "freely" = ______.   (1,5 marks)

III. WRITING (6 marks)
"Is globalisation good or bad for developing countries?" Write a composition (about 12 lines) giving your opinion, with advantages and disadvantages. Use linkers.
